chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Abdillah from Abi al-Jawzaa' from al-Husayn ibn Alwan from Mundhir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It was mentioned that Salman said: 'A man entered Paradise because of a fly, and another entered Hell because of a fly.' It was said to him, 'How is that, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'Two men passed by a people who were celebrating a feast for themselves, and they had placed idols for themselves. No one could pass by them unless he offered a sacrifice to their idols, whether little or much. So they said to the two men,
ai.seo_question: Why did one man enter Paradise for offering a fly while another entered Hell for the same act?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *Istidraj* and the value of sincere intention by contrasting two men who passed a tribe worshipping idols; one offered a fly as a token gesture, while the other refused to give anything to anyone but Allah and was martyred for his steadfastness. This narrative highlights that even a small act of compromise in worship can lead to spiritual loss, whereas total devotion to Allah, even if it costs one's life, guarantees Paradise. The story serves as a practical lesson on maintaining *Tawhid* in daily interactions with polytheistic practices.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Abi Abdillah from Abi al-Jawzaa’ from al-Hussain b. Alwan from Mundhir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

The narrator asked Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.), “O Master! How is it possible that a person goes to Paradise because of a house fly and another into Hell because of it?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “These two persons went to a tribe, which was celebrating a feast on that day. That tribe had an idol and none was allowed to go near it without offering a sacrifice. However there was no restriction on the size of sacrifice. The tribe refused to permit them passage unless they offered a sacrifice. One of those two persons said that he didn’t have anything to sacrifice. Then he caught a fly, killed it and offered it as a sacrifice while other companion refused to sacrifice even a fly for the sake of anyone except Allah. The tribal people killed him and he entered Paradise. On the other hand, the person who was left alive got punished in Hell.”
